easy.explain: Surahs 101 to 104. Al-Fil is 105, immediately after Al-Humazah.
Surahs 97 to 100. Al-Alaq is 96 and At-Tin 95, just before; Al-Qari'ah is 101, just after.

easy.set: The three prophets given kingdoms as well as prophethood
easy.explain: Yusuf was given authority in Egypt, and Dawud and Sulayman were given kingdoms. The decoys were prophets without temporal rule.

easy.set: The three prophets connected with Egypt in the Qur'an
easy.explain: Yusuf rose to authority in Egypt, and Musa and his brother Harun were sent to its ruler.

easy.set: The four things Muslims abstain from while fasting
easy.explain: The fast requires abstaining from food, drink and marital relations during daylight hours. Ordinary daily activity continues as normal.

easy.set: Four prophets mentioned as having been tested severely
easy.explain: Each of the four listed faced a well-known trial recounted in the Qur'an. The decoys describe blessings rather than trials.

easy.set: The three parts of the Islamic testimony of faith and action
easy.explain: The Hadith of Jibril explains Islam (outward submission), Iman (belief) and Ihsan (excellence in worship) in turn.

easy.set: Four of the prophets named in the Qur'an beginning with the letter Y
easy.explain: Four of the twenty-five named prophets begin with Y in the usual transliteration. The decoys all begin with I.

easy.set: The three categories of the hereafter mentioned in Surah Al-Waqi'ah
easy.explain: Surah Al-Waqi'ah divides people into three groups: the foremost, the companions of the right hand, and the companions of the left.

easy.set: Four cities significant in Islamic history
easy.explain: Makkah, Madinah and Jerusalem hold the three holiest mosques, and Damascus was the Umayyad capital.

easy.set: The three prayers recited aloud in congregation
easy.explain: The recitation is aloud in Fajr and in the first two rak'ahs of Maghrib and Isha. Dhuhr and Asr are recited quietly.

easy.set: Four companions known for narrating many hadith
easy.explain: The decoys are compilers of hadith from later generations, not companions who narrated them.

easy.set: Four months of the Islamic year, 1st to 4th
easy.explain: The year opens with Muharram, Safar and the two Rabi months.

easy.set: The three things said to continue benefiting a person after death
items: A righteous child who prays for them
easy.explain: A well-known hadith states that when a person dies their deeds end except for three: ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, and a righteous child who supplicates for them.

easy.set: Three acts performed during both Hajj and Umrah
easy.explain: Ihram, Tawaf and Sa'i are common to both. The decoys are rites of Hajj alone.

medium.set: The five obligatory prayers with the number of rak'ahs recited aloud
medium.explain: Recitation is aloud in Fajr and in the first two rak'ahs of Maghrib and Isha, and quiet in Dhuhr and Asr. Jumu'ah is recited aloud.

medium.set: Four surahs that open with praise of Allah (al-Hamd)
medium.explain: Five surahs open with 'Alhamdulillah': Al-Fatihah, Al-An'am, Al-Kahf, Saba and Fatir.
The decoys are wives of the Prophet ﷺ rather than daughters.

medium.set: Four companions who served as scribes of revelation
medium.explain: A number of companions wrote down revelation. The decoys were eminent companions known for other roles.

medium.set: Four surahs named after creatures or animals
medium.explain: Several surahs take their names from creatures. Al-Fath is the odd one among the decoys, being named for a victory rather than an animal.

medium.set: The four rightly-guided caliphs and the tribe they shared
medium.explain: All four Rashidun caliphs were of Quraysh. The decoys are companions from outside that lineage, reflecting the diversity of the early community.

medium.set: Four stages of the Qur'an's preservation
medium.explain: The Qur'an was memorised and written during the Prophet's life, gathered into one collection under Abu Bakr, and standardised under Uthman.

medium.set: Four surahs commonly recited for protection
medium.explain: Al-Fatihah, Ayat al-Kursi and the two Mu'awwidhatayn are widely recited for protection. Ayat al-Kursi is a verse rather than a surah.

medium.set: Four terms describing the Qur'an's own divisions
medium.explain: Surah, ayah, juz and hizb are divisions of the Qur'anic text. The decoys are terms from hadith study and exegesis.

medium.set: Four events that took place during Ramadan
medium.explain: Several major events fell in Ramadan, including Badr in 2 AH and the conquest of Makkah in 8 AH. The decoys took place in other months.

medium.set: Four of the prohibitions listed in Surah Al-Hujurat
medium.explain: Surah Al-Hujurat prohibits mockery, offensive nicknames, suspicion, spying and backbiting.

medium.set: Four companions appointed as governors or commanders
medium.explain: These four held significant appointments. The decoys pair real companions with posts they did not hold.

medium.set: The four main categories of water purity discussed by jurists
medium.explain: Jurists classify water by its purity and its capacity to purify. The decoys describe sources rather than legal categories.

medium.set: Four surahs revealed entirely in the Makkan period
medium.explain: Surahs 6, 7, 10 and 12 are Makkan; the decoys are Madinan.
The decoys were companions, not relatives of that degree. Of the uncles listed, Hamza and al-Abbas accepted Islam.

hard.explain: Exactly five surahs open with praise of Allah: Al-Fatihah (1), Al-An'am (6), Al-Kahf (18), Saba (34) and Fatir (35).

hard.set: The Musabbihat — surahs opening with glorification of Allah
hard.explain: The Musabbihat are the surahs opening with a form of tasbih, glorification of Allah. Different scholars count them slightly differently.
Surahs 35 to 39. Saba is 34, just before; Ghafir is 40, just after.
Surahs 40 to 44, the group often called the Hawamim for their shared opening letters. The decoys are surahs 45 to 48.

hard.set: Five companions appointed governors during the Rashidun period
hard.explain: Each of the five held a genuine appointment. The decoys pair real companions with posts they did not hold.

hard.set: Five of the Prophet's wives after Khadijah
hard.explain: The decoys are the Prophet's daughters. Note that Zaynab bint Jahsh, a wife, and Zaynab bint Muhammad, a daughter, share a name.

hard.set: The four surahs with exactly five ayahs
hard.explain: Al-Qadr (97), Al-Fil (105), Al-Masad (111) and Al-Falaq (113) each have five ayahs. Al-Ikhlas and Quraysh have four, and Al-Asr and Al-Kawthar three.

hard.set: Five of the ten promised Paradise who were not caliphs
hard.explain: Six of the ten were not caliphs; Sa'id ibn Zayd is the sixth. The decoys are eminent companions not named in that narration.

hard.set: Five surahs placed between 85 and 90 in the mushaf
hard.explain: Surahs 85 to 89. Al-Balad is 90, Ash-Shams 91, Al-Layl 92 and Ad-Duha 93.

hard.set: Five surahs placed between 90 and 95 in the mushaf
hard.explain: Surahs 90 to 94. At-Tin is 95, Al-Alaq 96, Al-Qadr 97 and Al-Bayyinah 98.

hard.set: Five early Muslims who migrated to Abyssinia
hard.explain: The decoys remained in Makkah with the Prophet ﷺ rather than joining the migration to Abyssinia.

hard.set: Five scholars and the works they are best known for
hard.explain: The decoys deliberately mismatch scholars with works by others.

hard.set: Five battles of the Rashidun period, in order
hard.explain: The decoys all took place during the Prophet's lifetime, before the Rashidun period began.

hard.set: Five of the Asma al-Husna concerning forgiveness and mercy
hard.explain: The names listed concern mercy and forgiveness; the decoys concern might, compelling power and justice.

hard.set: Five surahs of juz 30 with more than twenty ayahs
hard.explain: The longer surahs of juz 30 cluster at its start; the very short ones come near the end of the mushaf.
